risks.risk: CRITICAL: Havering is structurally insolvent without government bailout. It is on its THIRD consecutive Exceptional Financial Support / Capitalisation Direction (~GBP 70-77m for 2026/27, after GBP 32.5m in 24/25 and ~GBP 56.6m drawn in 25/26; cumulative ~GBP 200m+, all BORROWING at ~GBP 6m/yr servicing). The 2026/27 budget report states the council will need EFS to balance the budget and that if the Capitalisation Direction is NOT awarded to value, the S151 MUST issue a S114 report - a LIVE S114 TRIGGER. EFS is forecast through 2028/29.

The Wates 12 Estates joint venture (~GBP 1.1bn, 50:50 with Wates Residential, ~5,000 homes across 12 estates) carries the council's risk exposure; several schemes are 'under review' on cost grounds. A prime investigation target for the Regeneration portfolio.

Temporary accommodation cost explosion: households in nightly lets/hotels up from 3 (2020) to 300+, adding >GBP 8m/year net; homelessness approaches up ~50%; usable PSL stock ~750 -> ~400. Plus an adult social care complexity surge (1-2-1 high-needs packages 80 users/2.5m -> 236 users/9.6m; residential weekly cost GBP 630 -> 1,050).
